data_points.quote: Summing every ministry's individually stated tally in that table comes to 12,912 — not 11,679. The gap, 1,233 codes, is the scale of double- and multiple-claiming going on even among the codes DPIIT counts as resolved.

data_points.quote: The natural assumption about 495 unassigned tariff codes is that nobody could figure out which ministry they belonged to — genuinely ambiguous, multi-use, or newly created products falling through a real classification gap.
data_points.series: Residual List of HSN Codes

data_points.quote: HS 49119910, 'hardcopy (printed) of computer software,' is tagged with two probable ministries at once — Electronics and Information Technology, and School Education and Literacy — a single product DPIIT itself could not settle between two plausible regulators.
data_points.series: Residual List of HSN Codes

data_points.quote: A cluster of Chapter 49 codes — printed books, dictionaries and encyclopaedias, children's picture books, globes — are all proposed to the Department of School Education and Literacy, a ministry that does not appear anywhere in the formal 31-ministry table of codes actually accepted; it exists in this document only as an unaccepted suggestion.

data_points.quote: The Cabinet Secretariat should set a public deadline for resolving the 495-code residual list, with a default-assignment rule (e.g., the 'probable' ministry becomes the owner of record if no formal objection is raised within a fixed window)
